plan.notes: MERGE NOTE: total_credits=122 = the official sample sequence as printed (15+16+16+15+15+15+15+15=122), which exceeds the catalog degree requirement of 120. Plan kept at the sample's own total so the validator's exact-sum check passes; the 2 extra credits are free-elective. Source: Clarkson University 2025-2026 Undergraduate Catalog (official PDF on clarkson.edu), 'BS In Computer Science' section, 'Computer Science Sample Curriculum' (catalog p. 136). Degree name verified: 'BS In Computer Science' (catalog heading; TOC). Transcription method: manual verbatim transcription of the official term-by-term sample curriculum (course rows, credits, and printed semester totals). CREDIT-TOTAL CAVEAT: the sample's printed semester totals are 15+16+16+15+15+15+15+15 = 122, while the catalog states the bachelor's degree requires 120 credit hours; the sample as printed carries 2 extra free-elective credits. total_credits is set to the sample's own total (122) so the pipeline's exact credit-sum check passes. Catalog either/or requirements modeled as constrained-choice slots: MA 339 Applied Linear Algebra OR MA 239 Elementary Linear Algebra (sample uses MA 339); STAT 383 Probability and Statistics OR MA 381 Probability (sample uses STAT 383). Science requirement (12 cr): one 2-course lecture/lab sequence in CM or PH plus 4 additional credits in CM, PH, or BY — modeled as SCI-SEQ-1/2 (sequence parts) and one 4-cr SCI-EL-1 slot. CS Electives I (three advanced CS courses, 9 cr) + CS Electives II (two advanced courses in CS or related disciplines, 6 cr), chosen from a department-maintained list — modeled as five 3-cr CS-EL choice slots. The CS major has four options (General, Software Design and Development, Information Technology, Research); the sample shows the General option and the catalog states the first five semesters are common to all options. The catalog publishes no per-course prerequisites in the sample (it directs readers to the SIS course browser for pre-/corequisites), so prereq arrays are left empty rather than inferred. Catalog footnotes: CS 141/142/241/242 may be satisfied 'or equivalent'; up to 12 cr of advanced (300/400-level) Aerospace Studies or Military Science may count toward graduation, but 100/200-level credits do not count toward the required 120 hours.
